title: Conditional Compliance Shield: per-route retention caps & premium SLA pilot
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Background: Large enterprise customers have asked for a bundled compliance + SLA offering priced as an add-on, but they also want fine-grained observability retention controls to limit cost. This ticket scopes a pilot ("Compliance Shield") that combines: 1) a premium SLA tier (99.95% with error budget rules and faster incident response), 2) a compliance pack (security questionnaire assistance + audit-log retention options), and 3) per-route retention caps and sampling policies to control observability costs.

Objective: Run a controlled experiment with 10 pilot tenants to validate the pricing and gating model, measure unit economics, and exercise contract and security-questionnaire flows during sales. We want to learn elasticity of uptake, impact on support load, and whether per-route retention controls materially reduce observability costs without increasing false positives for alerts.

Scope of work:
- Product: define entitlement matrix (what features are in Compliance Shield vs baseline).
- Pricing: model a two-part price (flat monthly surcharge + usage-scaled observability credit).
- Contract & Sales: update enterprise contract templates and security questionnaire snippets for the add-on; define approval flow in procurement.
- Console UX: add per-route retention cap controls (sample rate, retention window) and a checkbox to opt into Compliance Shield.
- Billing & Metering: wire events for per-route retention usage into billing pipeline and enable credit buckets.
- Engineering: implement server-side enforcement of per-route retention caps, sampling hooks, and SLA alerting playbooks.

Gating logic: Customers must complete a security questionnaire (auto-filled sections where possible) and accept updated contract terms before the SLA takes effect. Per-route retention caps are enforced only after opt-in. Admin role required to change caps.

Experiment duration: 10 weeks (pilot configuration + 8-week data collection + 1-week wrap-up).

Risks: potential confusion on console controls, billing disputes around retained observability credits, increased support tickets during rollout. Mitigations include inline help, a two-week free trial for the add-on, and a dedicated pilot success contact from Solutions Engineering.
acceptance_criteria: Pilot signup flow works end-to-end for 10 tenants (Sign-up, questionnaire completion, contract acceptance).
Per-route retention caps can be set via Console and enforced server-side with sample-rate controls (0.1% - 100%).
Billing records reflect observability credit consumption and monthly surcharge for all pilot tenants in test billing pipeline.
SLA escalation and on-call playbook triggered correctly for simulated incidents during pilot (runbook exercises passed).
Product & pricing team have at least 3 recorded buyer conversations with willingness-to-pay signals and counter-offers.
rollout_plan: Week 0: finalize entitlements, pricing model, and legal language (contract + SQ snippets).
Week 1-2: implement Console UI for per-route retention and opt-in checkbox + backend enforcement.
Week 3: run internal canary (eng + security) to validate enforcement, billing, and questionnaire flow.
Week 4-11: onboard 10 pilot customers with Solutions Eng hand-holding; collect usage, support, and revenue signals.
Week 12: compile pilot report, recommended pricing adjustments, and go/no-go for wider release.
success_metrics: At least 4 of 10 pilots convert to a paid add-on within 30 days of trial (40% conversion target)
Average observability spend per-pilot reduced by >= 25% vs baseline when per-route caps are used
No more than 6 billing disputes across pilots (target <= 6)
SLA response time SLO met in 95% of simulated incidents during pilot
